{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**Prepared for:** Customer (internal) 
**Re:** Playbook review of Vendor's Master Services Agreement 
**Status:** Verified findings only

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Master Services Agreement against the playbook. The core risk-allocation provisions are strong and require no redline: Vendor's indemnity package (§ 20), IP and Customer Data ownership (§ 14), the mutual liability cap and Excluded Claims (§ 21), assignment and change of control (§ 24), the licence grant (§ 13), warranties and remedies (§ 19), transition assistance and data return (§ 11), insurance (§ 18), governing law and venue (§ 28), and the express no-minimum-commitment and no-non-compete confirmations (§§ 2.1, 12.3).

Seven items require action. Six are customer-burdening provisions that fail the playbook fallback — full-term exclusivity (§ 2.2), a customer-payable daily liquidated damages penalty (§ 7.6), an unlimited no-notice Vendor audit right with remote system access (§ 22.1), an open-ended MFN running against us (§ 7.2), a one-sided eighteen-month no-hire (§ 12.4), and a 180-day non-renewal notice window (§ 8.2). The seventh is an omission: the Agreement contains no termination-for-convenience right for either party across a fixed three-year term (§ 9).

We also note that §§ 2.2, 7.2 and 12.4 each contradict § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that we have made no exclusivity, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment. That internal inconsistency supports our position and should make several of these edits straightforward.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary of position |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20.1 (with §§ 20.2–20.5, 21.3) | Meets preferred position in full; IP indemnity sits outside the cap as an Excluded Claim. No redline. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14.1 (with §§ 13.2, 14.2–14.4, 15.1) | Meets preferred position in full; minor non-material notes only (payment condition, telemetry carve-out). No redline. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Compliant | § 21.1 (with §§ 21.2–21.3) | Single mutual cap at greater of 12 months' Fees or USD 1,000,000, with full Excluded Claims set. No redline. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 (with §§ 24.2–24.4) | Consent-free assignment for us; Vendor restricted. Asymmetric in our favour. No redline. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 2.2 | Sole and exclusive provider for the full term, no performance exit. Fails fallback; walk-away territory. Proposal: delete § 2.2. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 7.6 | USD 25,000/day for "any delay in providing a dependency"; no threshold, grace period or cap. Fails fallback; walk-away territory. Proposal: replace with schedule relief for Vendor. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13.1 (with §§ 13.2–13.4, 14.3) | Extends to Affiliates, contractors and Authorized Users; no at-will revocation. No redline. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 12.3 | Affirmatively preserves our commercial freedom. Benefits us; exclusivity and no-hire issues handled under their own rules. No redline. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Missing** | § 9 (Termination) | Only cause- and event-based rights across a fixed three-year term. Walk-away territory. Proposal: add § 9.4 Customer 30-day convenience right with pro-rata refund; confirm Vendor has none. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | **Deviation** | § 22.1 | Audit at any time without notice plus remote access to our systems. Fails fallback on frequency, notice and system access; walk-away territory. Proposal: once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, independent confidentiality-bound auditor, no system access. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28.1 (with §§ 28.2–28.3) | New York law, CISG disapplied, exclusive New York County jurisdiction; no arbitration. No redline. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | **Deviation** | § 7.2 | Unlimited MFN in Vendor's favour, no scope, product, duration or comparison limits; contradicts § 12.3. Fails fallback; walk-away territory. Proposal: delete. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § 2.1 (with §§ 7.1, 12.3) | No minimum quantity or purchase commitment; declining further orders is not a breach. No redline. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 12.4 | One-sided 18-month restriction covering any Vendor employee at any time, with no carve-outs, and an outright no-hire. Fails fallback; walk-away territory. Proposal: narrow to mutual 12-month non-solicit, services personnel only, with advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | **Deviation** | § 8.2 (with § 8.3) | Twelve-month renewal term and the § 8.3 uplift cap are acceptable, but the 180-day non-renewal window exceeds the 60-day fallback and the 90-day walk-away threshold. Proposal: shorten to 30 days plus a 60-day Vendor reminder; up to 60 days is an acceptable fallback. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 11.1 (with §§ 11.2–11.3, 16.5) | Six months' assistance at expiring rates, 30-day data return in machine-readable format, certified deletion. No redline. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19.2 (with §§ 19.1, 19.3–19.5, 6.1–6.2) | 90-day Deliverable warranty, Services conformity for the term, full remedy ladder, disclaimers do not cut back express warranties. No redline. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1 (with § 18.2) | Meets preferred limits including USD 5M cyber and privacy cover, plus one-year tail. No redline. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following provisions fall into walk-away territory under the playbook and must be resolved before signature:

1. **§ 2.2 — Full-term exclusivity.** Exclusive dealing for the entire term with no performance-based exit. We seek deletion; it also contradicts §§ 2.1 and 12.3.
2. **§ 7.6 — Customer-payable daily liquidated damages.** "Any delay" trigger with unbounded daily accrual, no materiality threshold, grace period or aggregate cap. The § 21.1 cap does not cure the mechanic and could still expose us to the greater of 12 months' Fees or USD 1,000,000.
3. **§ 22.1 — Unlimited no-notice audit with remote system access.** §§ 22.2–22.3 are already acceptable, so only § 22.1 needs rewriting.
4. **§ 7.2 — Open-ended Customer-side MFN.** Unlimited obligation to extend better third-party supplier terms; contradicts § 12.3. We seek deletion.
5. **§ 12.4 — One-sided 18-month no-hire.** Bars us from engaging any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term; contradicts § 12.3. We will narrow rather than delete, given the parties have bargained for some restriction.
6. **§ 9 — No termination for convenience.** No convenience right for either party across a fixed three-year term with 180-day non-renewal notice. Vendor equally lacks the right, so our ask is limited to a Customer-side 30-day right.
7. **§ 8.2 — 180-day non-renewal notice.** Exceeds the 90-day walk-away threshold, although the fix is mechanical and a window of up to 60 days is acceptable to us.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the seven action items, with playbook-referenced comments: delete §§ 2.2 and 7.2; replace the § 7.6 penalty with schedule relief for Vendor; rewrite § 22.1; narrow § 12.4 to the mutual fallback; shorten the § 8.2 notice window and add a Vendor renewal reminder; and insert new § 9.4.
2. **Lead the negotiation with the § 12.3 inconsistency.** Vendor's own acknowledgement that we have made no exclusivity, MFC, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment undercuts §§ 2.2, 7.2 and 12.4, and should let us clear three items with limited debate.
3. **Signal our fallbacks selectively.** We can accept a non-renewal window of up to 60 days (§ 8.2) and the narrowed mutual 12-month non-solicit (§ 12.4). We should hold firm on deletion of §§ 2.2, 7.2 and the § 7.6 daily penalty, on the § 22.1 audit limits, and on a Customer convenience right.
4. **Confirm the commercial position on § 9.4** with the business owner (notice period and refund mechanics, which track the existing § 10.2 refund provision) before we send.
5. **Take no action on the compliant provisions** listed above; they meet our preferred position and we will not reopen them."}
